name: Colosseum
desc: Gladiators fought here for free; you'll pay about $20 to stand where they did. Worth every cent of the someday fund.

name: Trevi Fountain
desc: Toss a coin, guarantee your return trip — cheapest travel insurance on Earth. Go after midnight when the crowds finally sleep.

name: Pantheon
desc: A 2,000-year-old concrete dome with a hole in the roof, still flexing on modern architects. A few bucks to stand under the sky.

name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
desc: Miles of papal loot ending under Michelangelo's ceiling. Your neck will ache. Your soul won't.

name: St. Peter's Basilica
desc: The biggest church flex in Christendom and it costs nothing to walk in. Dress code strict, awe unlimited.

name: Villa Borghese Gardens
desc: Rome's green rooftop — rent nothing, wander everything, and spy on the skyline from the Pincio ledge for zero euros.

name: Spanish Steps
desc: 135 steps of prime people-watching. Sitting's banned now, so strike a pose and pretend you're in a 60s film.

name: Campo de' Fiori Market
desc: Tomatoes and gossip by morning; by night the square swaps produce for spritz. Both shows are free to watch.

name: Gianicolo Hill
desc: Climb above Trastevere at sunset and watch every dome in Rome blush. A cannon fires at noon; your jaw drops for free.

name: Roman Forum
desc: Downtown of the ancient world, now a gorgeous pile of rubble you can stroll through. Emperors gossiped here. So can you.
